checks: The author expressly attributes1July2029 to Article6(8), without a stated assumption. Its following sentence uses the date to urge timely design and testing of a fee model. The exact Council text and German memorandum instead require18months after the designated delegated and implementing acts enter into force.

The German memorandum expressly says those acts are not yet available and gives separate2028and2030adoption deadlines. Neither deadline fixes actual entry into force, and adding18months only to the earlier one does not establish a final statutory commencement.

A strong benign interpretation remains a planning assumption about earlier adoption and coordinated entry into force, rather than an attempt to state a final date. Similar industry references to2029 do not themselves prove that assumption correct or incorrect.
No actual future acts schedule was established, so the screen cannot prove that application cannot begin in2029, that it must begin in2031, or that urgency is unnecessary.
Independent early national fee design, current recycling capacity and policy efficacy rationales are not adjudicated.
adjudication: Retain unresolved/minor/null. The statutory-attribution wording is worth clarification, but do not convert the conditional rule into a categorical later-date correction or a proved forecast error.
